name: Mochi
description: Mochi arranges every open window side by side so nothing overlaps, and you move between them from the keyboard.

hero.lede: Mochi arranges every open window side by side so nothing overlaps, and you move between them from the keyboard.
notes: Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit. No admin rights needed.
The moment it starts, every window becomes a tile. <kbd>Pause</kbd> turns tiling off and on, and <kbd>Alt+Shift+E</kbd> stops Mochi and puts every window back.
If Windows says it protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway.
hero.away: Mochi runs on Windows. Open this page on your PC to download it.

image.name: hero
image.alt: Four windows tiled side by side by Mochi, the focused one with a pink border

features.label: Layouts
features.title: Seven layouts, one key away
body: Mochi tiles in BSP, columns, rows, vertical stack, horizontal stack, ultrawide and grid. <kbd>Alt+Shift+V</kbd> steps through them.

main.name: f1
main.alt: The same four windows in the vertical stack layout

features.label: Workspaces
features.title: Nine workspaces on every monitor
body: <kbd>Alt+1</kbd> to <kbd>Alt+9</kbd> switch workspace, and <kbd>Alt+Shift</kbd> with a number takes the focused window along.
Each workspace keeps its own layout, so one can be in columns while another stays in BSP.

main.name: f4
main.alt: A second workspace with three windows in columns

features.label: Float
features.title: Float a window above the tiles
body: <kbd>Alt+Shift+Space</kbd> takes the focused window out of the layout and leaves it at its own size and place, above the others. Press it again to tile it.

main.name: f2
main.alt: A floating window above four tiles

features.label: Resize
features.title: Resize tiles from the keyboard
body: <kbd>Alt+Shift+S</kbd> enters resize mode: <kbd>H</kbd> and <kbd>L</kbd> make the window narrower and wider, <kbd>J</kbd> and <kbd>K</kbd> taller and shorter, and <kbd>Esc</kbd> leaves. The tiles next to it make room.

main.name: f3
main.alt: The left tile made wider in resize mode

features.label: Scripting
features.title: Every answer as JSON
body: mochic drives Mochi from a terminal or a script, and every command that reports something takes --json. mochic why says why a window is or is not tiled.
The hotkey file is plain text and is reloaded the moment you save it.

main.name: f5
main.alt: The hotkey file in a text editor and JSON answers from mochic in a terminal

assistant.label: AI assistant
assistant.title: Arrange windows by asking
body: mochic mcp lets an AI assistant see your monitors, workspaces and windows and arrange them: focus a window, move it, switch workspaces, set the layout.
No tool can stop Mochi, close a window or write a file, and nothing leaves your PC. Download the skill to teach your assistant the rest.
assistant.caption: Add Mochi to your MCP client (replace you with your Windows user name)

items: Mochi-Setup.exe: download, double-click, done. It adds Mochi to Installed apps, and Uninstall there removes it.
mochic mcp, a local MCP server for AI assistants.
mochic start --dry-run now runs in the terminal it was typed in.

requirements: No account and no internet connection

privacy.title: Nothing leaves your PC
body: Mochi makes no network connection and needs no account. The assistant connection uses the same local pipe as mochic.

data.title: Two plain text files
body: Settings live in %USERPROFILE%\mochi.json, hotkeys in %USERPROFILE%\.config\mochi\hotkeys. A log a day goes to %LOCALAPPDATA%\mochi, and the last 14 are kept.

keys_note: From the default hotkey file. Every key can be changed in it.

basics.title: Get started
steps: Click Install. Mochi starts and tiles every window.
Hold <kbd>Alt</kbd> and press <kbd>H</kbd>, <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>K</kbd> or <kbd>L</kbd> to move between windows.

basics.title: Updates
body: Download Mochi-Setup.exe again and open it. It stops the running Mochi first and leaves your settings and hotkeys alone.

basics.title: Removing it
body: Settings, Apps, Installed apps, Mochi, Uninstall. Every window goes back where it was. Your settings and hotkeys stay until you delete them.

a: Yes. It is free and open source under the GPL-3.0 licence.

faq.q: Why does Windows say it protected my PC?
a: Mochi is not signed with a paid certificate, so Windows warns about it the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway. Setup needs no admin rights and installs only for you.

faq.q: How do I get my normal desktop back?
a: <kbd>Pause</kbd>, or <kbd>Alt+F12</kbd> on a keyboard without a Pause key, turns tiling off and leaves every window where it is. <kbd>Alt+Shift+E</kbd> stops Mochi and puts every window back.

faq.q: A window is not being tiled. Why?
a: Run mochic why with that window in front. It says what Mochi makes of the window and what you can do about it. A program running as administrator cannot be moved, because Mochi runs without admin rights.

faq.q: Where does Mochi keep my data?
a: Settings in %USERPROFILE%\mochi.json, hotkeys in %USERPROFILE%\.config\mochi\hotkeys, and the log in %LOCALAPPDATA%\mochi. Nothing leaves your PC.

closing.title: Get Mochi
closing.sub: Free for Windows 10 and 11. No admin rights needed.
